mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and reduces profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 12-month maximum indicates a robust housing demand recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous 12-month maximum for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its previous 12-month maximum for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages signals a simultaneous expansion in employment and moderation in unemployment, indicating a healthy labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: An above-trend acceleration in real personal savings (RSAFS) for four consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining GDPC1, suggests a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer demand pullback and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months and GDPC1 is flat or declining.
